result_text:
I fixed the bit layout of the controller status byte (`DPTHVACStatus`) in `xknx/dpt/dpt_20.py`, so `0x21` now reads as Comfort instead of Night. I didn't run the test suite. I only checked with a short script that a `0x21` response now sets the climate device to Comfort/Cool.

The previous xknx release decoded the low nibble as the operation mode (`0x21` was Comfort, `0x22` Standby, `0x24` Night, `0x28` Frost Protection). The newer `DPTHVACStatus` decoder in 3.1.0 had the byte reversed. It treated the high bits as the mode, so `0x21` came out as Economy/Night, which Home Assistant shows as "Sleep".

The layout is now:

| Bit | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Comfort |
| 1 | Standby |
| 2 | Economy (Night) |
| 3 | Building protection |
| 4 | Dew point |
| 5 | Frost alarm |
| 6 | Inactive |
| 7 | Heat (1) / Cool (0) |

Both reading and writing the byte use this layout. Your `0x21` is Comfort with the frost-alarm bit set.

I took this layout from the old decoder's values plus my recollection of the Eberle status spec (AN097), not from the spec itself. Heat/cool is the least certain part. Your `0x21` has bit 7 clear, so it now reads as Cool. If the controller is actually heating, the heat/cool bit may be placed differently.

The existing tests for this DPT probably still use the old bit positions and will likely fail. I left them alone, as you asked.
